liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dear Mr. Fantasy** (2 reviews): Reviewer considers this one of the finest Dear Mr. Fantasy > Hey Jude jams; Reviewer values shows featuring Dear Mr. Fantasy > Hey Jude Finale [10][13]
- **Built To Last** (1 review, 1 other source): First version of Built To Last, with Jerry singing lyrics with zest; Built To Last played for the first time [1][13]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd88-10-20 t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd88-10-20 t02 Cold Rain & Snow**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd88-10-20 t03 New Minglewood Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd88-10-20 t04 Candyman**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd88-10-20 t05 Me & My Uncle**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd88-10-20 t06 Mexicali Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd88-10-20 t07 West LA Fadeaway**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd88-10-20 t08 Queen Jane Approximately**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-10-20.141656.schoeps.cmc3.mk41.pcm.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 23 songs; 138 min [1]
- **gd1988-10-20.152119.ultramatrix.healy-pearson.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 20 songs; 136 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]. Said about its sound: Cold Rain And Snow had low levels causing tape hiss on master [2]
- **gd1988-10-20.aud.dogman.gems.105858.flac16**: audience recording; 20 songs; 121 min; rated 4.11/5 by 9 [4]. Said about its sound: Rough audience tape, but Jerry's voice was good after East Coast tour [15]
- **gd1988-10-20.set2.akgC422.west.82488.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 11 songs; 65 min; rated 3/5 by 6 [7]. Said about its sound: Recording has a boomy, reverberant quality with mellow song versions; Levels and vocals were off; noise reduction avoided to preserve fragile vocals [7][8]

## Around the show

- The Summit venue is now a giant church, no longer hosting rock concerts [8]
- Reviewer was 17, stuck in Houston, and this was their only Dead show [9]
- Stories circulated about border roadblock vehicle searches during the tour [11]
- Friend wore a gas mask for smoke; security herded dancers back to seats [14]
- Reviewer was pulled over and friend slapped by police leaving Houston [17]
- Bobby and Brent looked in the zone from the fifth row [17]
- Joel Osteen angle makes the show seem strange and dreamlike decades later [19]
- Band likely avoided Astroworld, where they played in 1985 [8]
- First set was sleepy until The Music Never Stopped added sparkle [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-10-20.141656.schoeps.cmc3.mk41.pcm.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Source Info: Ted Mattes' Master Audience PCM (OTS); Schoeps CMC3/MK41 > Oade P/S > Sony PCM-F1 > Sony SL-2000; Transfer Info: PCM (Sony SL-10)> Sony PCM-601ESD… [1]
- **gd1988-10-20.152119.ultramatrix.healy-pearson.miller.flac2496**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  March 23, 2021; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MX-XG) [2]
- **gd1988-10-20.aud.dogman.gems.105858.flac16**: taped by Alan "Dogman" Miller; transferred by Jamie Waddell and Patrick White; source: AKG Microphones > Nakamichi550 1st Generation Maxell XLII-S Tapes ( the masters are gone ). [4]. Also: This first-generation tape replaces previous multi-gen copies and stands as surviving master [10]
- **gd1988-10-20.set2.akgC422.west.82488.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Todd Evans; source: AKGC422 > Sony D5 8ft high 30 ft center (or D5 tuned up and Nak300) [7]. Also: First circulating copy of this concert; DrumZ pause blended for seamless sound [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1988-10-20 Thu The Summit, Houston, TX](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1418818778739/grateful-dead-1988-10-20-thu-the-summit) [21]
